pairs.why: Same windmill build and finish in both; A's wheat is slightly chunkier and less fine-grained, which fits the smoother real cards a little better, but the gap is tiny.
Both have the same windmill, the same clean finish and clouds in the sky; the only difference is distant hills in A, which doesn't change how close either is to the real cards.
Same model, the same bare gradient sky with no clouds and nearly identical wheat texture; neither is closer to the real cards.
Nearly identical renders with bare skies and the same wheat density; nothing separates them against the real cards.
Same windmill, finish and empty sky in both; the differences are too small to matter.
Both have empty gradient skies and matching wheat and tower rendering; they are equally close to the real cards.
B has soft clouds and a distant horizon like the lighthouse card, so it reads as a staged game scene; A's bare sky and wall-to-wall wheat feel emptier and busier.
A has soft clouds and rolling hills behind the wheat, like the real lighthouse card's backdrop; B's bare sky and wheat over the whole lower half read busier and less staged.
